findings.evidence: `Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean:90) and `Algebra.semiringToRing` (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean:169) are reducible non-instances; putting them in a def body makes the term mention a structure that is only defeq, not syntactically equal, to `H`'s real one. The weakening buys no generality either — the PR reconstructs the `Ring` from `Semiring`+`Algebra k H` itself.
findings.fix: Declare the group/ring structure in the section `variable` block (`[AddCommGroup H]` / `[Ring H]`, as before this PR) so every definition and lemma uses the ambient instance and the `let`s, the `change`s, and the `@`-applications all disappear.
findings.issue: Definitions are built by tactic scripts that install a non-ambient structure instance into the term: `dualDistribEquiv` (:80), `evalTripleEquiv` (:136), `instFinite` (:63) use `letI : AddCommGroup H := Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup k`, and `evalLinearEquiv` (Functoriality.lean:182) uses `letI : Ring H := Algebra.semiringToRing k`. The PR then pays for this throughout: `Basic.lean:88` and `:145` re-introduce the same `let` just to make `rfl`/`simp` go through, `Functoriality.lean:191` and `:231` do the same, and `Functoriality.lean:301-311` needs two `change`s plus fully `@`-applied instance arguments to work around what its own comment calls "the finite-dual instance diamond".

findings.evidence: Functoriality.lean:303-311 spells out `bH.toCoalgebra.toCoalgebraStruct` / `bHH.toCoalgebra.toCoalgebraStruct` explicitly precisely because the inferred instances are not syntactically the ones `BialgEquiv.ofBijective` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Equiv.lean:330) selects.
findings.fix: Add a named `private theorem coe_evalBialgHom : ⇑(evalBialgHom k H) = ⇑(evalLinearEquiv k H) := rfl` and rewrite with it so the coercion defeq is isolated in one place; once the instance diamond from finding 1 is removed, write `evalBialgEquiv` in term mode as `BialgEquiv.ofBijective (evalBialgHom k H) h`.
findings.issue: `evalBialgEquiv` is a `def` whose body is a tactic script using `change` on its own declared type (:303-305) and again on the bijectivity goal (:308). The second `change Function.Bijective (evalLinearEquiv k H)` relies on the coercion of a four-layer bundled morphism (`BialgHom` → `AlgHom` → `LinearMap` → `LinearEquiv`) being definitionally the underlying `LinearEquiv`; the comment records what is done, not why no lemma is available. The tactic-built body then leaks: `evalBialgEquiv_apply` (:313-315) must `simp only [evalBialgEquiv, id_eq, ...]`, with `id_eq` present only to clean up the `let` artifacts.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn ofConv_mul_apply TauCeti` → only Basic.lean:427 (private, `[HopfAlgebra k H]` section) and its two uses at :497, :508; the new file duplicates the proof rather than reusing it.
findings.fix: Move `ofConv_mul_apply` into the `Bialgebra` section of `Basic.lean`, make it public (e.g. `ofConv_convMul_apply`), and derive both Functoriality.lean copies from it instead of re-running the induction.
findings.issue: The same argument — `rw [LinearMap.convMul_apply]; generalize Coalgebra.comul … = z; induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on` — is written three times in the repo after this PR: `convMul_apply_eq_dualDistribEquiv` (:234-245), the first calc step of `evalAlgHom.map_mul'` (:215-224), and `ofConv_mul_apply` (Basic.lean:436-445). The Basic.lean version already states the general fact but is `private` and stranded inside `section HopfAlgebra`, so neither new copy can reuse it.

findings.evidence: `grep -n symm_symm Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Equiv.lean Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Equiv.lean` returns no hits — there is no `BialgEquiv.symm_symm` lemma, so nothing but defeq is discharging that step.
findings.fix: Prove by extensionality instead: `BialgEquiv.ext fun phi => …` using `BialgEquiv.ofBialgHom_symm` and `BialgEquiv.coe_ofBialgHom` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Equiv.lean:301-306), or make the `symm_symm` step an explicit rewrite.
findings.issue: `mapEquiv_symm` ends `unfold mapEquiv; rw [BialgEquiv.ofBialgHom_symm]; congr 1`. After the rewrite the two sides differ by `map k e` vs `map k e.symm.symm`, so the bare `congr 1` closes the goal on the undocumented definitional equality `e.symm.symm = e` (plus proof irrelevance for the two `BialgHom` equation arguments). This is exactly the kind of accidental-defeq reliance that breaks when `BialgEquiv.symm` is refactored.

findings.evidence: `grep -c induction_on` on the new file gives 6, each with the same two-line `congrArg₂` add case; Basic.lean:307 shows `TensorProduct.ext'` is already the available idiom.
findings.fix: Where the statement is an equality of maps in the tensor variable, use `TensorProduct.ext'` (already used in this codebase at Basic.lean:307), which discharges the zero and add cases automatically; otherwise factor the add-case step into a single private helper and apply it at each site.
findings.issue: The identical add-case boilerplate `| add … => simpa only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply] using congrArg₂ (fun a b => a + b) …` is copied six times in the new file (:99-100, :118-120, :221-223, :242-244, :256-258, :275-277), together with the surrounding zero/add scaffolding.

findings.evidence: Functoriality.lean:63 and :87 are character-for-character the same statement modulo `mapLinear` vs `mapAlgHom`; :189 and :229 likewise for `evalLinearEquiv` vs `evalAlgHom`.
findings.fix: Prove them by delegation — `mapAlgHom_apply_apply := mapLinear_apply_apply k f phi x` and `evalAlgHom_apply_apply := evalLinearEquiv_apply_apply k H x phi` — as `map_apply_apply` (:131-133) already correctly does.
findings.issue: `mapAlgHom_apply_apply` (:84-88) is proved by a fresh `rfl` even though `mapLinear_apply_apply` (:61-64) already states the same equation one wrapper layer down; likewise `evalAlgHom_apply_apply` (:227-232) is a fresh `rfl` copy of `evalLinearEquiv_apply_apply` (:188-192). Each new `rfl` re-crosses the bundled-morphism coercion independently, so a change to `AlgHom`'s coercion breaks them all rather than one lemma.

summary: The PR builds definitions on `letI`-manufactured `AddCommGroup`/`Ring` instances, which forces undocumented defeq manipulation downstream: re-introduced `let`s before `rfl`, two `change`s inside the `evalBialgEquiv` definition, and a bare `congr 1`. It also re-proves an existing lemma twice and copies the same tensor-induction boilerplate six times.
